description:
Dynatrace automatically monitors process groups that are of known technology types or that consume significant resources. With process grouping rules, you can automatically monitor additional technologies.

For more information read the [community post](https://dt-url.net/ea2319k).
documentation: Process grouping rules also work for processes that have [deep monitoring enabled](https://dt-url.net/3203vvp).

standaloneRule.documentation:
If this option is selected, the default Dynatrace behavior is disabled for the detected processes. Only this rule is used to separate the process group.

If this option is not selected, this rule contributes to the default Dynatrace process group detection. 

[See our help page for examples.](https://dt-url.net/1722wrz)

id.description: This identifier is used by Dynatrace to recognize this process group.

name.description: If Dynatrace detects this property at startup of a process, it will use its value to identify process groups.

advancedSettings.description: Set advanced options to customize delimiters and control how property values are processed.
advancedSettings.documentation:
Consider an environment with processes such as:
 * `python myScript.py --env=prod12 --id=12`
 * `python myScript.py --env=dev2 --id=2`
 * etc.

 To group production *(prod)* and development *(dev)* processes together you could use Command line property with:
 * **Delimiter** from `--env=` to `--id` to extract `prod12 ` and `dev2 `
 * Enable **Ignore numbers** to transform `prod12` to `prod*` and `dev2` to `dev*`.

name.description: If Dynatrace detects this property at startup of a process, it will be matched to this grouping rule.

condition.description:
- $contains(svc) – Matches if svc appears anywhere in the process property value.
- $eq(svc.exe) – Matches if svc.exe matches the process property value exactly.
- $prefix(svc) – Matches if app matches the prefix of the process property value.
- $suffix(svc.py) – Matches if svc.py matches the suffix of the process property value.

For example, $suffix(svc.py) would detect processes named loyaltysvc.py and paymentssvc.py.

For more details, see [documentation](https://dt-url.net/j142w57).

constraints.customMessage: Should have one of the following formats: $prefix(parameter), $eq(parameter), $suffix(parameter), $contains(parameter)

caseSensitive.documentation: When enabled, matching conditions are case sensitive. When disabled, matching conditions are case insensitive

name.documentation: When this field is empty, OneAgent will automatically assign the process group name based on process type and properties like executable name. If you expect that multiple processes will be matched by the rule, it is highly recommended that you fill this field because it is unspecified which process will be used as the group name source.
